name: Agent request to a built result, checklist and live code
looks: A short request types into a chat panel on the left. Beside it a checklist of tool calls ticks off one by one, each gaining a green check as it completes, while a code editor on the right types the real output line by line. The editor's result then renders beneath as a small UI preview, which grows from a single card into a row of three.
build: The chat request and the editor code both use terminal-type-on's per-character reveal, on two offset clocks so they feel like two live panels, not one. Each checklist row's icon swaps from a loading ring to a check on its own beat, top to bottom. The preview card's row uses variant-stack-reveal to go from one panel to three, staggered and settling square.
sound: A key tick under both typing panels, a soft blip per checklist item completing, and a cluster of settle hits as the preview cards land.
prompt: Show an AI agent doing real, visible work: a short request types into a chat panel, a checklist of the steps it takes ticks off one by one, and a code panel beside it types the result live. Finish on the rendered output building from a single element into a small set, proving the request became something real.
